steps.text: Ashen skies. Strong winds. Untamed wilds. Somber graves.
This is the final resting place for all High Inquisitors.
Irene still remembers the sight, from the first time her master brought her here.
What she dared not tell him at the time was that it had made her heart burn with a zealous sense of purpose. That to her, their sacrifice was something to be glorified.
That she had felt as if the entire graveyard was shrouded in a hallowed beauty.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (It's so beautiful...)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Irene.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Oh! Y-Yes, Maestro!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Seeing as you've chosen to become my deputy, then starting today, I am not just your teacher, but also your superior officer.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: This is where my mentor brought me when I first became an Inquisitor.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Most of the graves here are cenotaphs. After all, not many in our line of work are recovered in one piece when we die.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: So rather than their bodies, their lanterns and weapons better represent the trail they've cleared in life.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: As such, we place them here on the graves of every Inquisitor to fall in battle, to serve as a memorial.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: And these nine tombstones... are for the nine Saints.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Nine? But isn't your master, Lord Carmen, still alive?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: While the other eight have long since perished on their journey, Lord Carmen has already designated this as his final resting place.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (How wonderful would it be if I could give my life defending Iberia and be buried here too.)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Irene.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: One day, you will also bring my lantern and weapon here, to lay them to rest.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: I can only hope that when that day comes, you will not grieve, but rather have understood what we fight for.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Because by then, nobody will be left to instruct you.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Until that day, though, I will teach you everything I know.
Irene remembers answering with a resounding 'Yes, sir!'
But at the time, she did not understand the weight of her master's words, nor the weight of a life.
She did not understand. Not until after everything she experienced on the Stultifera, not until she was carrying her master's tools with her to lay upon his grave.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: There are more graves here now.
Irene arrives in front of one.
'Here sleeps High Inquisitor Dario.'
A simple wooden plaque. A single, unassuming sentence, with no embellishments. The grave of a High Inquisitor.
Lest she disturb his soul, she gingerly places what he left behind on his grave, before slowly sitting down.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Maestro, I've brought your lantern. I've brought your weapon.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: As you requested, I've returned them to your grave, so that your soul may return to your homeland.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But, even though I made that promise back then, I never thought the day would come so soon.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: While it's been some time since it happened, I still can't believe that you're no longer with us.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But in the end, you're gone.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: There will be nobody to scold me for being childish. Nobody to warn me to think more, to observe more. Nobody to shelter me from the wind and the rain.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Never mind. If you could hear me now, I'm sure you'd just chide me for being soft and weak.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Don't worry. I still remember what you said. That you hoped I would understand what we are fighting for.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I think I do now. At least somewhat.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So... I might not be back to visit you for a while.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Not because I've lost faith in my beliefs.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: If anything, I'm doing this because I now truly understand the meaning of 'inquisition.'

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I hope you can continue to watch over me, Maestro.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Lord Carmen?!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: No need to be so nervous. I am nothing more than a teacher, come to see his fallen student.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Those items you placed belonged to Dario, no?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Y-Yes. While it didn't need to be me who brought them here, I wanted to do it myself.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: He was my maestro after all, and... I wanted to tell him goodbye.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Oh?

The person standing before her eyes is a High Inquisitor crowned with the title of Saint. Every Inquisitor knows of the countless trials Saint Carmen has overcome, and of the countless evils he has passed his judgment on.
His existence itself is the embodiment of the Inquisition's will.
For a moment, she regrets the decision she has made, but quickly suppresses that thought.
She made up her mind long ago.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I handed in my resignation before coming here.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I plan to step down from my position as Inquisitor. So, I wanted to say goodbye to my maestro before I leave the Inquisition.
Irene had already prepared answers to the questions she was sure would come, but is met only with the Saint's silence.
She dares not speculate what this silence implies, but does not sense any anger from him.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Dario was my eighth student, and the finest of them all.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But he was never very good with words, and wasn't particularly popular even among the Inquisitors. He never stopped calling me 'Lord' either, even though I was his teacher.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: It must not have been easy being his student.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That's not true.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Maestro always acted swiftly and decisively. I admired that about him, and the results proved again and again that he was always correct.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Only thanks to the many, many mistakes he made when he was younger.
A fleeting illusion flashes across Irene's mind—that the person in front of her is not a strict and stolid Saint, but rather a weary old man.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Had I accompanied him to the Eye of Iberia, he would likely not have given his life.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Aboard that golden ship, when that monster told me news of his passing, she told me that his death was meaningless.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So I responded: 'the Inquisition never makes sacrifices in vain.'

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But before he died, he once taught me that the notion of a good death was nothing but a romanticization.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That for us Inquisitors, the only way we can fulfill our ideals is by living on.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So before considering whether his death was meaningful or not, it would've been better had he survived. That's what I've been thinking.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Dario taught you well.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: After the calamity swept over Iberia, the other Saints and I gradually grew the Inquisition into what it is now.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We achieved a great number of things, most of which can be read in the Scriptures.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But sometimes, I've been forced to ask the very same question: had I acted differently, could I have prevented someone's death? Countless deaths?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Ultimately, I am but one man. Even if different choices could have allowed me to do so much more, they too might've resulted in yet more death.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: In other words, there's only so much one person can do.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Surely you're not resigning because you're disillusioned in the direction the Inquisition is going?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Of course not... I didn't expect you to see through me so easily, though.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Had that been the case, you would've shied away from me after you returned from the Stultifera.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But you didn't.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Your convictions now are even purer than when I first saw you in Gran Faro.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: What reason would I have to suspect you of running away?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I still remember a few years back, when Dario told me that he would take his first student. A young child.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: For the survival of the organization, each High Inquisitor must select a few students from among the Inquisitors, and pass down everything they have learned.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: However, it is extremely rare for one to choose a child.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The Scriptures saved my life, but had Maestro not been there, I may well have still died in those ruins.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: After that, I was taken to the Inquisition's orphanage, and he occasionally came to see me from then on.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...It's not as if he became my maestro right away. Actually, as a High Inquisitor, it was against regulations for him to instruct an orphan like me in the first place.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But some time after he found out that I wanted to become an Inquisitor, and had already begun training for it, he suddenly told me that he wanted to personally teach me a few things.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: His decision always puzzled me too, so I eventually found an opportunity to ask him about it. I'll never forget what he said.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You want to know why I decided to take you as my student?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Because your zealotry for the Inquisition, the Scriptures, and the Law reached my ears.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: And that is your fatal flaw.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Your justice comes from the texts that saved you, from the Inquisition that raised you, from your own studies in your path to becoming an Inquisitor.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: But it leaves little room for the sights witnessed with your own two eyes, the words heard by your own two ears, or the ground tread by your own two feet.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You are still too fragile, Irene.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I didn't understand him at the time, and he wasn't willing to say anything more, so I always just kept his words in the back of my mind.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I never understood what he meant, until now.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: He feared that I would be blinded by justice, hurt by zealotry, and slain too soon by truth.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Because I was so convinced that the contents of the Scriptures and the Law made me who I am.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: So, you began to wonder if there are limitations to our laws.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: No, I'm still convinced that the Law is effective.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Then you want to say that the distinction we make between good and evil lacks nuance.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: No, I believe that our codes are tried and true.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: In that case, why are you leaving the Inquisition?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Maestro once told me that when the time comes, I must become Iberia's last line of defense.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I used to think he expected too much of me, but now I see that this was the least he could have hoped for.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It wasn't because of any special talent of mine, or because I'm to fulfill some kind of unique duty.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It was because he expected the same of himself, and he did just that.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So as his student, it was only natural that I do the same.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Everything I learned on the Stultifera, everything he ever taught me, was all to help me to come to one realization—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That the Scriptures and the Law will guide my actions, but my actions must first abide by my own ideals.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I must first understand myself. Have faith in myself. Only then will the Scriptures and the Law truly grant me strength. Only then will my lantern truly strike fear into the sea monsters.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I witnessed the truth in the cage beneath the Inquisition. And on the Stultifera, I learned of their thoughts, their language, and... their evolution.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I have seen our enemies clearly, and now understand the imminent crisis we face.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I have traveled with the Hunters, and fought alongside them. I have seen their pride, but also the extent of their strength.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: They are unknowns, but we need not fear them.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: So, my child, after everything you've experienced, what is the answer you've arrived at?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: When I came face-to-face with those monsters, it became immediately clear that what I suspected was what Maestro also suspected. That what I feared was what he also feared.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: My justice could not endure the trial I faced, and my maestro's conviction was the result of thorough consideration.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I will no longer doubt, hesitate, or run. I will do what I can do. What I must do.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Lord Carmen. I should've chosen my words more carefully.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: But please believe me. I'm stepping down only so that I can better carry out my duties as an Inquisitor.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The position of Inquisitor is an extremely sensitive one. Only by relinquishing it are you able to work with other organizations, or even countries.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Child, you've witnessed the light of multilateralism.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: So what will you do after parting ways with the Inquisition?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'll try to work with the three Abyssal Hunters for the time being.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: They seem to have close ties to that Rhodes Island organization, so I am considering whether or not to reach out to them.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Hmm, if that's the case...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Did you hear all that, Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Huh?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Sorry, but the conversation had gotten so interesting that I couldn't help but stop and listen in.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Naturally, Rhodes Island would never refuse the assistance of such a capable Inquisitor.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Irene, you can step down without leaving the Inquisition altogether, you know.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You can become our Messenger to Rhodes Island, and cooperate with them on our behalf.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Remember, Irene. Your decision today will be the next step in Ægir's partnership with Iberia.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: ...Yes, sir!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Good. Get ready to set off then.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Nobody will be there to guide you on your new journey. Only the faith in your heart can show you where to go.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: See, Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: For me, the opportunity for Ægir and Iberia to rejoin hands came far, far too late.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Even if they've given us an opportunity to turn things around, time has taken its toll on me, and I can no longer feel even the slightest bit of joy from it.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But for her, it truly is the dawn of a new day.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If their evolution is the instinct of life itself, then the decision she made just now must surely be the instinct of civilization.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: What are you looking at?

a.text: The old man follows Kal'tsit's gaze. The lantern resting atop Dario's grave suddenly flickers a few times.
As if it is saying both goodbye, and good luck.
